value: Mrs. Agatha Sowerby resides at Sowerby's Hollow
unit: Residing at Sowerby's Hollow in Brierley with her husband Thomas, Mrs. Agatha Sowerby spent her days keeping diligent watch over the neighborhood thoroughfare while managing various church organizations. When Nell Harcourt first arrived at Grey Shutters, Mrs. Sowerby visited after recovering from influenza and made sharp remarks about Nell's plain appearance and red hair, provoking a passionate outburst from the young girl. Though initially offended, she forgave Nell after receiving a humbled apology. Over the following years, she offered advice to Thirza and Obed Abernethy regarding Nell's upbringing, made dresses for Nell, and attended church and community events, including winning first prize for butter and cheese at an exhibition. Although she expressed doubts about Nell's character and opposed women's higher education, she eventually praised Nell's growth and personal development while remaining pleased when Nell gave up plans to attend college.

unit: Isolde Pembroke grew up at Pear Hill and became the bosom friend and schoolmate of Nell Harcourt after returning from a visit to her aunt in Delford. The pair spent their days playing at their playhouse, Larkrise, and sharing a seat at school. When Mrs. Pembroke temporarily forbade Isolde from playing with Nell after an accidental drunkenness incident involving currant wine, Isolde loyally sent Nell secret gifts and notes. After the misunderstanding was resolved, their close bond resumed, including shared adventures, school recitations, writing club activities, and a trip to town to visit her Aunt Lavinia for the Exhibition. Though Isolde was not enrolled in the Regent's entrance class alongside Nell, she remained Nell's most devoted companion, comforting her through hardship and continuing their close friendship.

unit: Isolde Pembroke grew up at Pear Hill and became the bosom friend and schoolmate of Nell Harcourt after returning from a visit to her aunt in Delford. The pair spent their days playing at their playhouse, Larkrise, and sharing a seat at school. When Mrs. Pembroke temporarily forbade Isolde from playing with Nell after an accidental drunkenness incident involving currant wine, Isolde loyally sent Nell secret gifts and notes. After the misunderstanding was resolved, their close bond resumed, including shared adventures, school recitations, writing club activities, and a trip to town to visit her Aunt Lavinia for the Exhibition. Though Isolde was not enrolled in the Regent's entrance class alongside Nell, she remained Nell's most devoted companion, comforting her through hardship and continuing their close friendship.

Following Obed's sudden death from a stroke, Nell chose to forgo her scholarship to stay at Grey Shutters, accepting a local teaching post in Delford to support and care for Thirza.

unit: Obed Abernethy resided at Grey Shutters in Brierley with his sister Thirza. Facing advancing age, poor health, and a shortage of farm labor, he and Thirza arranged to adopt a young boy from an asylum. When Obed drove to Alder River station to collect the child, he discovered that an orphan girl, Nell Harcourt, had been sent by mistake; unable to tell her the truth, he brought her home. Though he was notoriously afraid of young girls, he quickly became fond of Nell and quietly insisted on keeping her. Over the next four years, Obed formed a deep friendship with Nell, encouraging her studies and taking immense pride in her accomplishments, including her winning of the Avery scholarship. He eventually passed away, leaving Nell and Thirza grieving his loss.

value: Mr. Pidgeon served as the schoolteacher at the Brierley schoolhouse.
unit: Mr. Pidgeon served as the schoolteacher at the Brierley schoolhouse. During his tenure, he focused much of his instruction on older students like Sukey Pullen while largely ignoring younger children. He frequently disciplined pupils like Nell Harcourt by making them stand at the front of the room, while overlooking minor misconduct from others. Under the guise of assisting Sukey with her studies for the Regent's examination, he visited her home almost every night. On a school outing, he gathered Mayflowers and presented them to Sukey. At the end of the term, he delivered an emotional parting speech to his class before leaving his teaching position.

unit: Thirza Abernethy resides at Grey Shutters alongside her brother Obed. Having arranged to adopt an orphan boy to assist on their farm, they receive Nell Harcourt by mistake; though initially intent on rectifying the error through Mrs. Tranter, Thirza ultimately decides to keep and raise Nell. She instills discipline, homemaking skills, and proper decorum in the imaginative girl, despite frequent domestic mishaps involving baking disasters, ruined pudding sauces, and mislaid wine. Over time, Thirza grows deeply attached to Nell, supporting her education through high school. She attends political gatherings in Port Marlow as a Conservative supporter and remains an active participant in the local Aid Society. When Obed's heart condition worsens and he eventually collapses and dies, Thirza draws comfort from Nell, expressing the maternal love she had long kept guarded beneath her stern exterior.
